card.name: News report points before official sources
card.fires_on: Sentence-end punctuation, a closing quote, or a linking word in news stories about outbreaks, disease or attacks, right where an official source or agency is likely to be named next.

modes.label: Sentence end before an agency
modes.description: A period or closing quote ends a news sentence, and the next sentence is likely to cite an agency or expert.
modes.example: long-term sun exposure accumulated over many years may be equally harmful<<. >>The U.S. Centers for Disease Control

modes.label: Nationality or link word in outbreak news
modes.description: A nationality adjective, comma or 'and' in an outbreak report, just before 'health authorities' or a count of cases.

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words like 'authorities', 'Gov' and 'experts', which name official sources.
card.plain: It fires in news stories about outbreaks or health findings, at a point where the writer is about to name officials or experts.
